items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: a boy named Sidney DeParis says, 'I'm the greatest trumpet,' everybody's saying, 'I'm the greatest trumpet in America.'

ctx.x: He's got a funny way of laughing. "Now, I think I'll play another one." And he played a thing called "Slew Foot Stomp." And when he got through that third chorus, and people was standing up on the tables, and Rex grabbed a man's derby and tore it up, the man come out with something, a razor, wanted to get in -- "Here's your $10.00." They calmed the man.

And that was it. That was it. That was it, man. And that was the end of everybody challenging Louis Armstrong after that. But they had a lot of people doing these things. One time in the Rhythm Club, they heard him in there and I think it was -- Rex couldn't get there then, a boy named Sidney DeParis says, "I'm the greatest trumpet," everybody's saying, "I'm the greatest trumpet in America." And then they got down to the greatest trumpet in New York. Then they got down to the greatest trumpet in Harlem. 132nd…
